verses.verse:
मुखरन्ध्रे विनिक्षिप्तः फूत्कारो घर्षको भवेत्।
तेन घृष्टोऽचलो वायुस्तेन नादः प्रजायते।६७।
verses.text: Sent into the mukharandhra (mouth-hole), the phūtkāra (breath) becomes the rubbing [agent]; the still air, rubbed by it, gives rise to nāda (musical sound).

commentary.text: So, for sound to arise in any bānsurī, the rubbing air, that is, the phūṅk (breath), must be slanting. If the flow of the rubbing [air] becomes strong, the vibration of the air begins to increase in the order of twofold, threefold and fourfold. This action cannot be seen with the eyes, but as a result of these actions the ears hear in the sounds the difference Sa Ṡa Ṗa Ṡa. So we infer that in the enclosed air inside the bānsurī the capacity to vibrate takes many forms, depending on the length of the bānsurī. So with slackness or strength in the flow of the breath, the capacity changes at once. Now, leaving this subtlety to the scientists, I must move on to the elements that concern the practice of music. So, about the qualities of the breath in the bānsurī —
